findings.evidence: Spec says to reuse 'the wrapper's existing Assert-NotInsideRepo-style guard (~codex-dispatch.ps1:452-466) or the same detection'. The live guard (codex-dispatch.ps1:455-465) first runs [System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($Path), swallows any CreateDirectory failure with `return`, and signals a violation by throwing, not by returning a result. Line 84 says 'Do not create the missing root before this check', and line 104 tests 'no root creation'.
findings.summary: The guard cannot be used as-is for this check. Validation runs before the provisioning gate, so calling the guard creates the missing root and the 'missing root -> exit 72, no root creation' case fails. For a real root inside a worktree it also leaves a directory in the judged tree. A CreateDirectory failure makes it silently pass. A throw would take the launch-setup failure path (exit 1), not the required exit 72 refusal. The spec should require a non-creating detection: walk up to the nearest existing ancestor and run `git -C <ancestor> rev-parse --show-toplevel`. It should map a hit to the exit-72 unsupported-root refusal, and the suite should assert the root is absent after refusal.

findings.evidence: Regex `^[A-Za-z]:\\[A-Za-z0-9_.\\-]+$` excludes `~`, spaces and other characters. The default root is Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'codex-sandbox-tmp'. Line 100 builds the suite root under [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath().
findings.summary: The regex is valid in PS 5.1 and the trailing `-` is literal. It will refuse every default launch when the user profile path contains a space (for example `C:\Users\John Smith`). It will also refuse a test area under an 8.3 short-name temp path such as `BENJAM~1`. This works for the current profile (`User`). If the refusal is intended, the SKILL.md row should say so. The suite could also fail cleanly or skip when GetTempPath is itself unsupported.

findings.evidence: The live row 187 reads '... NOTHING was launched and NO ledger row exists.' The draft requires the provisioning gate after the lease opens (line 85: 'The lease is already open at this gate') and also tells the row to 'Keep the existing ... preflight ledger semantics'.
findings.summary: The provisioning refusal leaves a lease and close event, so 'NO ledger row exists' is wrong for it. The unsupported-root refusal for read-only or fake launches has unspecified placement relative to the lease. Task 2 should say the new causes differ on ledger semantics. The Task 2 apex-accept check only tests terms (baseline, spec, sandbox temp, provision, New-Item, icacls), so it passes the contradictory text. The current row lacks four of those terms, so the check fails until the edit lands, as intended.

findings.evidence: Suite cases cover a missing root and a root with no qualifying ACE. None covers a qualifying Allow ACE passing, or a Deny ACE disqualifying it (the round-3 note, carried forward).
findings.summary: The ACE pass path and the Deny rule have no automated check. H3 covers the pass path live. Previously accepted.
